jd:
SRIYOG is an information technology consulting organization focused on helping clients solve complex digital challenges. The team works on a range of technology projects, from modern web solutions to software platforms that support business growth. Interns at SRIYOG gain exposure to real-world client work, collaborative problem-solving, and industry-standard tools. The company values continuous learning, practical experience, and innovative thinking in its technical talent.


Role Description 
The Frontend Developer Intern role at SRIYOG is a remote internship position focused on building and improving user-facing web interfaces. Day-to-day tasks include implementing responsive layouts, translating design mockups into functional web pages, and collaborating with developers to integrate frontend components with backend services. 


The intern will help troubleshoot UI issues, optimize performance, and ensure cross-browser and cross-device compatibility. This role also involves learning best practices in frontend development, participating in code reviews, and contributing to documentation for ongoing projects.


Qualifications
 

- Candidates should possess skills in Front-End Development and Responsive Web Design to create accessible, user-friendly interfaces.
- Candidates should possess skills in Web Development and Back-End Web Development to collaborate on full-stack features and integrations.
- Candidates should possess skills in Software Development to apply sound coding practices, debugging, and version control workflows.
- Familiarity with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript (and common frameworks or libraries) is highly beneficial.
- Strong problem-solving abilities, attention to detail, and willingness to learn in a remote, collaborative environment are expected.
- Enrollment in or completion of a degree or certification in Computer Science, Information Technology, or a related field is preferred but not strictly required.


Note : This is not a paid opportunity.
fit_why: Frontend web intern matches React, TypeScript, JS, full-stack experience

jd:
Teamwork makes the stream work.

Roku is changing how the world watches TV

Roku is the #1 TV streaming platform in the U.S., Canada, and Mexico, and we've set our sights on powering every television in the world. Roku pioneered streaming to the TV. Our mission is to be the TV streaming platform that connects the entire TV ecosystem. We connect consumers to the content they love, enable content publishers to build and monetize large audiences, and provide advertisers unique capabilities to engage consumers.

From your first day at Roku, you'll make a valuable - and valued - contribution. We're a fast-growing public company where no one is a bystander. We offer you the opportunity to delight millions of TV streamers around the world while gaining meaningful experience across a variety of disciplines.

About The Role

Join Roku as an Engineering Intern and help build the agentic AI powering America’s #1 TV streaming platform. Roku reaches more than 100 million households worldwide, and we’re building production-grade AI agents across the products and platforms that serve them. We offer a paid 12-week internship, running from June to early September 2027.

As an Engineering Intern, you’ll be assigned a scoped project with one of our engineering teams and matched to the team that best fits your skills and interests. You’ll work on real problems, such as agents that investigate failures, automate workflows, review or generate code, or help people make complex decisions. You’ll learn how to take an AI-powered idea from prototype to something people actually use, with a mentor alongside you and real ownership from day one.

Our teams work across a variety of languages and technologies, from user interfaces and embedded software to platform services, automation and developer tooling, and embrace AI-assisted development to boost productivity and quality.

What you’ll be doing



- Own a well-defined project that contributes to the success of your team, from defining the problem through to delivery.
- Build and test AI agents, copilots and automated workflows that perform meaningful, multi-step work.
- Connect agents to trusted data, services and internal tools, using approaches such as retrieval, tool calling and orchestration, and help define what an agent may do on its own and when it should hand over to a person.
- Evaluate your work: measure whether it does the job well, check its reliability and failure modes, and keep improving it based on real feedback.
- Use AI coding tools every day to move faster, and validate everything they produce through testing, review and your own judgment.
- Write clean, well-tested, documented code, take part in code reviews, and collaborate with engineers, mentors and cross-functional partners.

Apply if



- You are a penultimate-year student, or a final-year student planning to go on to a one-year master’s course.
- You hold a permanent right to work in the US. Unfortunately, we are unable to consider candidates on a student visa.
- You are available for full-time work for the whole 12-week program, from June to early September.
- You are keen to work with AI technologies and have previous experience building AI agents and automated workflows.

We’re excited if you have



- Currently enrolled in a degree program in Artificial Intelligence, Computer Science, Engineering or a related field.
- Proficiency in Python, ideally with projects, open source or hackathon work beyond your coursework.
- Hands-on experience building an LLM-powered or agentic system that does multi-step work, and ideally that someone other than you has used.
- Familiarity with agentic patterns such as grounding and retrieval, tool use, orchestration, memory or conversational interfaces.
- Sound engineering judgment: you check AI-generated work, understand how it can fail, and recognise when simple automation or a human review is the better approach.
- A solid grounding in computer science fundamentals such as data structures, algorithms, and operating systems or networking concepts.
- Strong problem-solving and technical communication abilities, and the ability to break down ambiguous problems and deliver in small steps.
- Proactive mindset with passion for continuous learning and fast iteration.

How will I use AI at Roku?

At Roku, we don’t just use AI, we work with it. AI agents and smart tools help power drafts, analysis, and repetitive workflows, while our people bring direction, judgment, and accountability. We’re looking for curious, adaptable builders who can show how they’ve used AI or automation to move faster, raise the bar, and scale their impact.

We value your AI skills if you have built fluency across the agentic engineering toolchain — coding harnesses like Claude Code or Cursor, MCP servers, custom skills, or agent frameworks. You know how to drive an agent, verify its output, and ramp on an unfamiliar codebase with an agent helping you.

What's Roku's approach to hybrid working?

Roku fosters an inclusive and collaborative environment where teams generally work in the office Monday through Thursday. Fridays are generally flexible for remote work, except for employees whose specific roles or assigned office location require five days' a week attendance.

What are some of the benefits?

Roku is committed to offering a diverse range of benefits as part of our compensation package to support our employees and their families. Our comprehensive benefits include global access to mental health and financial wellness support and resources. Local benefits include statutory and voluntary benefits which may include healthcare (medical, dental, and vision), life, accident, disability, commuter, and retirement options (401(k)/pension). Employees are supported in taking time off, in accordance with local leave policies and other personal needs to support their evolving work and life needs. It's important to note that not every benefit is available in all locations or for every role. For details specific to your location, please consult with your recruiter.

Accommodations

Roku welcomes applicants of all backgrounds and provides reasonable accommodations and adjustments in accordance with applicable law. If you require reasonable accommodation at any point in the hiring process, please direct your inquiries via email.

What should I know about Roku's culture?

Roku is a great place for people who want to work in a fast-paced environment where everyone is focused on the company's success rather than their own. We try to surround ourselves with people who are great at their jobs, who are easy to work with, and who keep their egos in check. We appreciate a sense of humor. We believe a fewer number of very talented folks can do more for less cost than a larger number of less talented teams. We're independent thinkers with big ideas who act boldly, move fast and accomplish extraordinary things through collaboration and trust. In short, at Roku you'll be part of a company that's changing how the world watches TV. 

We have a unique culture that we are proud of. We think of ourselves primarily as problem-solvers, which itself is a two-part idea. We come up with the solution, but the solution isn't real until it is built and delivered to the customer. That penchant for action gives us a pragmatic approach to innovation, one that has served us well since 2002.
fit_why: Strong AI agent fit; Python, RAG, LLM work; US-based role

About Our Internship ProgramZoox's internship program offers hands-on experience with cutting-edge technology, mentorship from some of the industry's brightest minds, and the opportunity to make meaningful contributions to real projects. We seek interns who demonstrate strong academic performance, engagement beyond the classroom, intellectual curiosity, and a genuine interest in Zoox's mission.

Job DescriptionThe Software Systems organization builds the foundations that the autonomy and product software run on, and the systems that verify that software. Interns gain an end-to-end view of the Zoox software stack while solving a focused problem on one of the teams below. Interns in this pipeline may be considered for opportunities across a range of teams, including:
Systems Engineering: Builds simulation-based and model-based checks that catch software defects early in the development pipeline.
Software Performance: Profiles and optimizes runtime latency and resource use across the stack.
Software Core: Develops the middleware, networking and sensor tooling that connect vehicle software components.
Product Security: Strengthens the security of the vehicle and its software, including remote attestation.
Simulation: Builds machine learning-based sensor simulation, reconstruction and world models used to test the driving software.


In this Role, You Will...:
• Design and implement software for a defined project, such as a profiling tool, a network scheduler, an automated checker or a simulation component 

• Evaluate design options through experiments, benchmarks or literature review 

• Test and document your work so the team can adopt it 

• Present results to engineering stakeholders at the end of the summer

Requirements:
• Currently working towards a B.S., M.S., Ph.D., or advanced degree in computer science, computer engineering, electrical engineering, or a related engineering program 

• Expected to graduate between Fall 2027 and Summer 2028, and enrolled at an accredited college or university throughout the internship 

• Able to commit to a full-time, 12-week internship beginning in May/June 2027 

• Ability to relocate to the Bay Area, California, for the duration of the internship 

• Interns at Zoox may not use any proprietary information they are working on as part of their thesis, any published work with their university, or to be distributed to anyone outside of Zoox

Qualifications:
• Experience programming in C++ or Python 

• Understanding of operating systems, networking or computer architecture fundamentals 

• Familiarity with modern software development practices (Git, unit testing, CI) 

• Enthusiasm for automotive technologies and robotics 

• Strong interpersonal and communication skills

Bonus Qualifications:
• Experience with simulation frameworks used in robotics 

• Experience with performance profiling, low-level systems programming or network protocols 

• Machine learning, security or 3D graphics experience, depending on team

Compensation
The monthly salary range for this position is $6,500 to $9,500. Compensation will vary based on geographic location and level of education. Additional benefits may include medical insurance and a relocation stipend. 


About Zoox
Zoox is developing the first ground-up, fully autonomous vehicle fleet and the supporting ecosystem required to bring this technology to market. Sitting at the intersection of robotics, machine learning, and design, Zoox aims to provide the next generation of mobility-as-a-service in urban environments. We’re looking for top talent that shares our passion and wants to be part of a fast-moving and highly execution-oriented team.

Follow us on LinkedIn

Accommodations
If you need an accommodation to participate in the application or interview process please reach out to accommodations@zoox.com or your assigned recruiter.

A Final Note:
You do not need to match every listed expectation to apply for this position. Here at Zoox, we know that diverse perspectives foster the innovation we need to be successful, and we are committed to building a team that encompasses a variety of backgrounds, experiences, and skills.
fit_why: Systems/robotics SWE; C++/Python fit, but autonomy and robotics specialty gap

About Our Internship Program
Zoox's internship program offers hands-on experience with cutting-edge technology, mentorship from some of the industry's brightest minds, and the opportunity to make meaningful contributions to real projects. We seek interns who demonstrate strong academic performance, engagement beyond the classroom, intellectual curiosity, and a genuine interest in Zoox's mission.
 
Job Description
Autonomy Software builds the software that lets the Zoox robotaxi perceive its surroundings, predict what others will do, and plan and control the vehicle with no one behind the wheel. Interns join one of the teams below, work with a mentor on an open research or engineering question, and see a direct path from their work to the system that runs on Zoox vehicles and in simulation.

Interns in this pipeline may be considered for opportunities across a range of teams, including:
Autonomy Behaviors: Owns the decision-making, planning & control modules, which decide how the vehicle drives. Projects include machine-learned planning, long-horizon reasoning, configurable driving styles, freeway driving and new vehicle platform bring-up.
Perception: Gives the vehicle an understanding of its surroundings using camera, lidar, radar and audio. Projects include object detection and tracking, multimodal foundation models, scene understanding, occupancy and 3D mapping.
Guidance & Routing: Works on route-level planning and offline mapping, including the mission planner, map data delivery and road network tools.
Collision Avoidance System: Runs an independent safety layer with its own perception and planning. This team also works on the evaluation and data tooling for verification.


In this Role, You Will...:
• Work on interesting research or advanced engineering problems that could have the potential to revolutionize the existing Autonomy Software stack. 

• Design, build and evaluate state-of-the-art algorithms or machine learning models for a real autonomous driving system. 

• Train and test models on large-scale driving and simulation data, and analyze failure modes to measure improvements. 

• Write production-quality C++ and Python that goes through code review. 

• Present your results to your team and at the end-of-summer project showcase, and contribute to publishable research where the project allows.

• Experience in at least one of machine learning, computer vision, motion planning, controls, prediction or mapping
